meta.medium: Acrylic paintings, giclée prints, video, installation
meta.subtitle: Digital Exhibition

text: Kristóf Szabó aka KristofLab presents his most critical project yet, Artificial Paradise. His practice explores the relationship between nature and civilisation, wilderness and urbanisation, and man's artificially created habitat: the city and its symbol, the tower block.

Artificial Paradise takes this further: artificially created natural spaces, domesticated and industrialised nature. Visions of the future that seemed utopian a few decades ago (a new relationship between nature and man, the possibility of total control) have become everyday practice.

Controlled, industrialised nature calls into question the very definition of nature. Can we still speak of nature when vegetation is artificially created and sustained, and functions as a visual element? How does this affect ecology and our image of nature?

KristofLab uses his usual multimedia tools (installations, videos, paintings and collages) to explore the bizarre, alienating nature of the phenomenon, and to envision the possibilities encoded in its present.
textCredit: Text by Luca Cserhalmi, aesthete. The exhibition was opened by Barabás Zemlényi-Kovács, theorist and independent curator.
behindTheScenes: A reconstruction, not an invention. The floor plan is traced from the gallery's own room sheet, photographed on the wall by the bar, and its overall length matches the building's outline on OpenStreetMap. Room 1 is measured from a 360° panorama: solving the camera position from the corners and the four canvases of known size gives the room's real size, the recess around the doorway and where the windows, the screen and the plant stood. Every painting hangs at its listed canvas size and measured height. The brick on the walls is cut from the photographs: a script measures the 7.7 cm brick courses for scale, divides out the gallery lighting and stitches each patch so it tiles along the mortar joints. The artworks are perspective-corrected crops, and the screens show the frames caught on camera. Paradise Factory and the plastic river of Let it Flow are modelled from the photos. Three.js and Vite, no backend; the room tone is synthesised with Web Audio.

r1.name: Room 1
r1.subtitle: Paintings · Paradise Factory
r1.blurb: Down the stairs: four large acrylic paintings (Wrong Data Landscape Dresden, Human as Error I, III and VI) and Paradise Factory, the hydroponic installation in the middle of the room.

r2.name: Room 2
r2.subtitle: Video · bar
r2.blurb: The bar room: the videos Artificial Paradise I and II, a table and chairs, and the small bar used at the opening and finissage.

r3.name: Room 3
r3.subtitle: Paintings · prints · video
r3.blurb: The Artificial Paradise giclée prints, three Wrong Data Landscape paintings and the 4K video Wiena Wrong Landscape II on the grey wall.

r4.name: Room 4
r4.subtitle: Let it Flow · video
r4.blurb: Open to Room 3 between two wall stubs and a curtain: Let it Flow, with Wiena Wrong Landscape I and Natural Life on the side walls.

w01-dresden.caption: Cyan and lilac blocks of corrupted data slide across a Dresden housing estate and a sunlit meadow; a thin red strip runs where city and field meet.

w02-human-as-error-vi.caption: A half-ruined tower block under a marbled sky, its base sinking into dense green brushwork and turquoise interface bars.

w03-paradise-factory.medium: Installation: hydroponic PVC pipe, seedlings, LED lights, plant on a drip feed, screen
w03-paradise-factory.caption: Lettuce seedlings grow in a white PVC pipe under an LED tube, hung from the ceiling on chains. In the middle of the room a plant is kept alive in a clear plastic tank, fed from a hanging bottle and lit by two vertical LED bars; a small screen on the wall shows a pixelated loop.

w03-screen.medium: Video on a small screen, part of the installation
w03-screen.caption: The monitor beside the hydroponic line: slow, vertically smeared blues and greens, like a feed from inside the plant factory.

w04-human-as-error-iii.caption: A prefab façade swallowed by a pixel-sharp canopy of green: the windows are still there, the building is disappearing.

w05-human-as-error-i.caption: Houses on a hillside smeared into a slope of earth and grass, cut off at the bottom by flat violet and green blocks of data.

w06-artificial-paradise-i.caption: A split screen of managed nature: orchids under grow lights, glasshouse struts, geodesic domes and artificial trees.

w07-artificial-paradise-ii.caption: The hexagonal glazing of biodomes, a waterfall, ivy and a leaf beaded with water, cut into a grid.

w08-wiena-wrong-landscape-ii.caption: A skyline rebuilt from corrupted image data: cyan towers, magenta blocks and smeared façades on the grey brick wall.

w09-warsaw-g24-i.caption: Pink and teal planes of a Warsaw tower block stacked over a grey, textured strip of vegetation.

w10-warsaw-ii.caption: A violet tower against a dark sky; a white tree and cyan ground break up into pixels at the bottom.

w11-artificial-paradise-i-print.caption: Singapore's Supertrees: steel trunks planted with ferns and climbers, a garden built as infrastructure.

w12-artificial-paradise-ii-print.caption: Glass towers rising behind manicured hedges, the sky smeared by a glitch.

w13-artificial-paradise-iii-print.caption: A black-and-white sculpture of curling fronds over a wall of planting, cut into blocks.

w14-warsaw-g24-ii.caption: A magenta tower block on pale blue ground, a dark tree pixelating at its foot.

w15-wiena-wrong-landscape-i.caption: A city front on open water; buildings slip into red and pastel glitch columns above the waves.

w16-let-it-flow.caption: Trees are projected across the end wall of the dark room. Out of the projected forest a river of crushed plastic (bottles, cups, bags, wrappers) winds across the floor.

w17-natural-life.caption: Ferns on a forest slope, filmed close up, on the black brick wall of the projection room.

source: Titles, sizes, media and years from the room sheet displayed in the gallery (photographed in DSC_0049).
